audit.why: Neither champion threatens a kill before 6: Nasus just farms and Tryndamere has no burst yet, so 1-4 are Skill (the mirror reached the same conclusion for rows 2 and 3 but skipped the edit believing the length band blocked enum tokens — it does not). Two items in, stacked Siphoning Strike plus tank stats invert the lane.
audit.corrected: Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Nasus with ratings 5,5,5,5,7,6,2; difficulty raised to 8/10 and the tone moved off green. The content whys already described exactly this shape — only the win tokens disagreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was marked Skill and 2+ items marked Tryndamere, inverting both real spikes.
audit.why: Undying Rage (120/100/80s, no cost) lands before Nasus has any fight tool, making 6 the widest window of the lane. Fury of the Sands is his, on the same 120/100/80s, and only gets stronger with stacks.
audit.corrected: 6 and first item are Tryndamere's; 2+ items is Nasus's, with the reason stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told you to 'cancel his Q Siphoning Strike animation', and never said what Fury of the Sands does to your defensive build.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset (7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s, 255 range) — the wind-up is the tell, and you deny the stack by taking the minion, not by interrupting him. Fury of the Sands batters nearby enemies for a share of max health while granting him bonus Armor and Magic Resist, so raw armour is the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: mid rewritten around the auto-reset tell and minion denial; spikes[3] now names the max-health damage.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Nasus's Wither is down.
edits.after: Nasus has no engage and you have no burst, so this is a farm race. Deny casters — every stack denied is damage he never gets.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wither's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Wither runs 15/14/13/12/11s — that gap is your only clean window. Between them, spend your time on his caster minions, not on him.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage arrives before he owns a single fight tool — this is the widest window of the lane. All-in while Wither is down; every Flash you force delays his stacking.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nasus carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: It inverts here: Fury of the Sands hands him resists and max-health damage, and stacked Siphoning Strike out-trades your crits.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wither and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 8/10. The lane is decided by how hard you deny stacks early, because he outscales you.

edits.before: From 3 to 6 it's a skill test of stack-denial: your job is to E in and cancel his Q Siphoning Strike animation on caster minions whenever it's up, keeping his stacks low while he has no answer until Wither and R come online.
edits.after: From 3 to 6 it's a skill test of stack-denial: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset on 7.5s at rank 1, so the wind-up is your cue — E in and take the caster minion off him, keeping stacks low until Wither and R arrive.

edits.before: Once Nasus completes his tank items and a few hundred Q stacks, his Wither slow plus R Fury of the Sands armor lets him tank your crits and one-shot you back — avoid extended fights and split away from him, forcing side-lane pressure instead of dueling.
edits.after: Once Nasus completes his tank items and a few hundred Q stacks, Wither plus R Fury of the Sands hands him bonus Armor and Magic Resist while battering you for a share of your max health — stacking armour will not save you. Split away from him instead of duelling.

notes: The page shipped diff 'HARD' beside diffRating 4/10, a green tone and 'Favoured matchup' — three fields disagreeing with each other and with a 43.59% win rate over 975 games. Mocking Shout (W) is worth knowing here and is already implied by the mirror: 14s cooldown, it cuts the Attack Damage that Siphoning Strike scales off, but its slow only lands on enemies whose backs are turned, so disengage from Wither facing him.
